title: Squeezing and Decoherence of Axion Dark Matter
abstract: Bosonic particles beyond the Standard Model, such as axions, are among the leading candidates for dark matter. If such particles have a small mass, they are usually described as a purely classical field. However, it was recently shown that this description is incomplete: their inherent gravitational self-interactions can squeeze the field, producing a quantum feature beyond the classical description. Here we analyze squeezing of light dark matter in the presence of decoherence. We show that squeezing is continuously generated, and rapidly enough to survive dissipation, and may also remain present under thermal fluctuations and dephasing. Our results demonstrate that dark matter might possess persistent quantum features and motivate further investigation of their implications for dark matter detection.
summary: This paper analyzes the quantum behavior of axion dark matter, showing that its self-interactions generate quantum squeezing in the field fluctuations. By analyzing the system as an open quantum system, the authors demonstrate that this squeezing is robust and can survive environmental decoherence, suggesting persistent quantum signatures for dark matter detection.
main_problem: The paper investigates whether the quantum features, specifically squeezing, inherent in axion dark matter fields survive environmental decoherence and dissipation.
main_result: The analysis shows that the non-linear self-interactions of the axion field generate squeezing rapidly enough that it can persist even in the presence of decoherence mechanisms.
method: The authors employ open-system analysis techniques to study the time evolution of quantum field operators, comparing unitary (closed-system) dynamics with dissipative evolution.
model_or_system: The system models axion-like particles as a highly occupied bosonic field whose dynamics are governed by a Kerr oscillator Hamiltonian, $\hat{H} = \hbar\omega\hat{a}^\dagger\hat{a} + \hbar\chi\hat{a}^\dagger^2\hat{a}^2$.
key_observables: Squeezing (quantified by quadrature variance $V_{-}(t)$), Wigner function evolution, and the time evolution of field moments ($\langle a(t) angle, \langle a^2(t) angle$).
important_parameters: Axion mass ($m$), non-linearity strength ($\chi$), and decoherence rates (related to the environment/bath).
main_assumptions: The initial analysis relies on the mean-field approximation, and the extension to decoherence requires modeling the system as an open quantum system interacting with a bath.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the evolution of the Wigner function showing nonlinear shearing and squeezing, and plot the onset and maximum magnitude of quadrature squeezing as a function of axion mass.
paper_structure: The paper first establishes the Kerr oscillator model for the axion field, demonstrates the initial squeezing via unitary evolution, and then extends the analysis to incorporate various decoherence channels to test the robustness of the quantum features.
why_interesting: This work directly bridges quantum optics (squeezing, decoherence) with fundamental particle astrophysics (dark matter), providing a theoretical framework for detecting non-classical quantum effects in cosmological fields.
